name: Kyrgyz Manas epic-recital (UNESCO 2013)
lineage: Kyrgyz Manas heroic-epic recital tradition recognized as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage 2013 (originally proclaimed 2009) under the inscription "Epic culture, folk tales and music of the Kyrgyz epic Manas". The Manas trilogy — Manas, Semetey, Seytek — reaches up to 553,000 verse-lines in the canonical recension. Classical manaschi epic-reciter performs voice-only with hand-gesture and cadence patterning, often in near-trance state; the akyn improvising sung-poet variant accompanies with the komuz three-string fretless lute. Sometimes shamanic in framing — the manaschi receives the epic in dream-summons from the spirit of Manas. Twentieth-century canonical figures include Sagymbay Orozbakov (1867-1930), Sayakbay Karalaev (1911-1971, whose recension is the largest documented corpus and whose portrait appears on the 500-som banknote), and contemporary Talantaaly Bakchiev (born 1971). Bishkek State Manas Theater established as state-level performance venue. Distinguished from Turkic dastan traditions by the Kyrgyz-language-specific narrative-cadence grammar and the trance-summons performance framing; distinguished from Kazakh kuy by voice-led (vs instrumental-led) tradition structure
